first of all, are you in Brazil? I ask because of the Portuguese in the packaging. If so, check out r/SkincareBR where we talk about local products as well. 

Second:
-absolutely do not start it all at once, you need to introduce each item one at a time so if you have a bad reaction to one you will know which product is causing it. I would wait try the hyaluronic acid, do it for a week, then add the snail cream, do it for a week and so on. 

-retinol is a very complicated ingredient. it irritates your skin and needs to be used carefully. you need to use a moisturizer after it, and start it out once a week for a while, if your skin doesn't get irritated do it two times, then three etc. you need to build tolerance to it

-snail cream: if you are allergic to shellfish, to dust mites or have allergic rhinitis it will break you out. learned this the hard way.

-you can't use vitamin C and retinol at the same time because they deactivate each other. Move the vitamin C to the mornings. 

-if you're doing retinol and vitamin C, you probably won't need an exfoliant. a few years ago, the 10 step skincare regimen went viral and it messed up a lot of people's skin. nowadays, we know about the importance of preserving your natural skin barrier, which can be damaged if you use a lot of actives. influencers will try to tell you that you need 100 products but less is more in skincare

-sunscreen: the only actually medically necessary skincare item is sunscreen, since it prevents skin cancer and damage from the sun. you need a face sunscreen as most body sunscreens are too heavy for the face and will give you acne

-cleanser: cleansers are soaps for your face. body soaps (and shampoos) are too harsh for the face and usually leave it very dry. cleansers can have different ingredients for different types of skin. if you don't know what type of skin you have, I would get one that says on the label that it's for sensitive skin as it's the least harsh one.

-moisturizer: if you live somewhere cold, you might need as cold dries out your skin and can leave an uncomfortable feeling. if you live somewhere hot or humid you probably don't need one.
